features.calculus_section: 4. Feature atlas - input representation and interface / Tokenizer / segmentation (C,S,P)
features.exact_definition: An input compiler T mapping a surface byte/character stream u to a symbol sequence tau_1..tau_n over a finite vocabulary Sigma, with |T(u)| = n(u) the token count. Subword schemes (BPE-style merges, unigram-LM segmentation) define T by a learned merge/score table fitted to a corpus; the induced map is generally many-to-one on surface forms and one-to-many on meanings.
features.experiment: B2.1 tokenizer granularity (factorial: surface morphology complexity x vocabulary size x sequence-length price x embedding memory price)
features.gmi_type_note: C because T fixes what counts as an atomic symbol for every downstream mechanism; S because it determines the state-table index set; P because n(u) multiplies every per-token training and serving cost.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Meter tokens, not characters or documents: report n(u) per corpus alongside every loss, or a tokenizer change silently rebuys the compute budget. Charge the embedding+unembedding parameter count to ΔB_mem separately from the body.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Byte-level or character-level input with a learned pooling/downsampling layer reproduces the sequence-shortening mechanism without a fixed merge table; a fixed hash n-gram vocabulary reproduces the table-size mechanism without learned merges.
features.kill_condition: A single vocabulary size/segmentation wins on sample efficiency AND serve tokens AND memory across corpora with materially different surface morphology, at matched model and token budget. That would falsify the no-universal-tokenizer claim of gap G-T01.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: T controls the length n(u) of the dependency chain the router must span AND the fragmentation of a semantic unit across positions; a unit split over k tokens requires k-step composition that a single-token encoding gets for free.
features.name: Tokenization / segmentation
features.negative_twin: Same model, same corpus, same token budget, but a tokenizer whose merges are drawn from a DIFFERENT corpus's statistics with the identical vocabulary size and the identical mean n(u): the size/length mechanism is held, the alignment mechanism is removed.

semantic_invariance.not_preserved: Per-token arithmetic: character-level counting, digit arithmetic, rhyme/phonology and byte-level edit distance are NOT invariant because tokens partition the surface differently; token-level probabilities are not comparable across tokenizers.

features.calculus_section: 4. Feature atlas - input representation and interface / Vocabulary size (C,S,P)
features.exact_definition: The cardinality |Sigma| = V of the token alphabet. It fixes the embedding matrix E in R^{V x d}, the unembedding W_U in R^{V x d}, the softmax partition over V logits, and (through the segmentation that produced it) the expected sequence length E[n(u)], which for subword schemes falls roughly as V grows with diminishing returns.
features.experiment: B2.1 tokenizer granularity (vocabulary-size axis)
features.gmi_type_note: C/S because V is the size of the discrete state table the compiler exposes; P because 2Vd parameters and a V-way softmax are charged at every step of training and serving.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Charge 2Vd parameters to ΔB_mem and the V-way softmax to ΔB_serve EXPLICITLY; a 'parameter count' that excludes the vocabulary heads makes a large-V model look cheaper than it is.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: A factorized or hierarchical (two-level) softmax with the same V reproduces the alphabet size while changing the materialization cost; adaptive-span embeddings reproduce the frequency-matching mechanism without changing V.
features.kill_condition: The optimal V is shown to be independent of the embedding/serving price vector at matched corpus and model size.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: V trades sequence length (a routing-depth and serve-cost term) against vocabulary-head materialization (a memory term) and against per-type sample efficiency; the optimum is where the marginal length saving equals the marginal table cost at the registered prices.
features.name: Vocabulary size
features.negative_twin: Hold V fixed and randomly REASSIGN which merges are in the vocabulary (same V, same table size, same softmax width, worse alignment to corpus statistics): the materialization cost is identical and the frequency-matching mechanism is destroyed.

resource_effect.direction: Larger V raises ΔB_mem (2Vd) and the per-step softmax cost, lowers ΔB_serve through shorter sequences, and degrades ΔL_gen for rare types through fewer updates each.

semantic_invariance.not_preserved: The parameter/compute SPLIT between the body and the vocabulary heads, and the effective sample count per token type: rare types get fewer updates as V grows.

features.calculus_section: 4. Feature atlas - input representation and interface / Embeddings (S,C)
features.exact_definition: A lookup E: Sigma -> R^d, tau |-> E[tau], realized as a V x d matrix read by one-hot indexing, supplying the initial residual coordinate r_i^{(0)} = E(tau_i) + p_i. It is a free-parameter table, not a computed function of the symbol.
features.experiment: MLX-41 probe vs causal-use separation (whether an embedding direction a probe finds is the one the model uses)
features.gmi_type_note: S because it is the coordinate system in which every later mechanism reads the input; C because it is the interface between a discrete alphabet and a continuous state.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Charge Vd parameters to ΔB_mem; when embeddings are tied to the unembedding (TF-033) charge the table ONCE and say so, or the same memory is double-counted or double-discounted across comparisons.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: A learned linear map applied to a fixed one-hot or hashed sparse code computes the same function class; factorized embeddings E = AB with A in R^{V x k}, B in R^{k x d} reproduce the lookup with a rank constraint.
features.kill_condition: A causal intervention shows that per-coordinate embedding semantics is preserved under an arbitrary invertible reparameterization absorbed into W^Q/W^K/W^V, which would contradict the gauge non-invariance stated here.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: The embedding geometry determines which token distinctions are CHEAP for downstream linear routing: distinctions aligned with large singular directions of E are separable by one linear read, others require depth.
features.name: Token embeddings
features.negative_twin: Replace E by a FROZEN random matrix with the same shape and the same row norms: the coordinate-supply and materialization mechanisms are held, the learned-geometry mechanism is removed.

features.calculus_section: 13. Small-feature closure table / embedding dimension (S/P)
features.exact_definition: The width d of the residual stream r^{(l)} in R^{n x d}. It fixes the rank ceiling of every per-position linear read (at most d independent linear features can be read without interference), the parameter count of every block (Theta(d^2) per projection), and the per-token FLOPs (Theta(d^2) per linear layer).
features.experiment: B2.7 MLP width/gating (width axis) and MLX-31 model/data/compute scaling surface
features.gmi_type_note: S because d is the dimension of the shared workspace all mechanisms read and write; P because every cost in the block scales as d^2.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Report d together with depth L and the token budget; 'parameters' alone hides that the same count buys different interference profiles at different (d, L) splits.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Depth-for-width substitution at matched parameters, or a low-rank bottleneck inside each block with a wide residual stream, reproduces the capacity change with a different cost signature.
features.kill_condition: A width that is optimal independently of the registered memory and compute prices, or a demonstration that feature interference never binds at any d for a fixed obligation.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: d is the capacity of the shared state through which all mechanisms communicate; raising d reduces read interference between concurrently carried features at quadratic cost.
features.name: Embedding dimension / model width d
features.negative_twin: Hold d fixed and hold total parameters fixed but SPLIT the residual stream into two non-communicating width-d/2 streams: the parameter and FLOP budget is matched and the shared-workspace mechanism is removed.

features.calculus_section: 4. Feature atlas - input representation and interface / Positional mechanisms (S,R)
features.exact_definition: A free table P in R^{n_max x d} added at layer 0: r_i^{(0)} = E(tau_i) + P[i]. Each position index i < n_max owns an independently learned vector; positions i >= n_max have no defined encoding.
features.experiment: B2.2 positional necessity and geometry (arm: absolute)
features.gmi_type_note: S because it writes order information into the residual coordinate; R because downstream attention scores read it to select by position.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Charge n_max x d to ΔB_mem, and charge the cost of ANY position-extension procedure (retraining, interpolation) to ΔB_update rather than reporting only the extended context length.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Sinusoidal positions (TF-006), rotary positions (TF-007), a relative bias (TF-008), or a causal-mask-plus-depth construction that reconstructs position from prefix counting all supply the necessary order information.
features.kill_condition: An exact side-channel-free realization with a fully permutation-invariant internal state satisfies an order-sensitive obligation. X-TMT1 enumerates the collisions that make this impossible at its scope.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Absolute position is supplied as content in the residual stream, so the router reads order through the same linear machinery it uses for token content; this makes order cheap to condition on and expensive to generalize across offsets.
features.name: Learned absolute positional embeddings
features.negative_twin: Bag-of-tokens: the identical model with P set to zero, so no order information reaches any layer. TMT-1 / X-TMT1 predicts exact failure on the order-sensitive obligations and NO change on the permutation-invariant one.

features.calculus_section: 4. Feature atlas - input representation and interface / Positional mechanisms (S,R)
features.exact_definition: A FIXED (unlearned) map p_i[2k] = sin(i / 10000^{2k/d}), p_i[2k+1] = cos(i / 10000^{2k/d}), added to the token embedding. Because each frequency band is a rotation, p_{i+delta} is a fixed linear function of p_i for every offset delta, which is the property the learned table lacks.
features.experiment: B2.2 positional necessity and geometry (arms: absolute / relative / rotary-like) and the long-extrapolation task
features.gmi_type_note: S/R for the same reason as TF-005, with the difference that the encoding is a closed-form function of i rather than a table.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Zero memory cost is real, but charge the extra attention capacity spent reconstructing relative offset from two absolute codes rather than reading it directly (TF-008).
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Rotary embeddings (TF-007) apply the same rotation idea multiplicatively inside the QK bilinear form instead of additively at layer 0; a learned table initialized to the sinusoid and frozen is a third realization.
features.kill_condition: Sinusoidal encoding extrapolates to indices far outside the trained range with no degradation at matched training, which would make the 'defined but not calibrated' distinction vacuous.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: The multi-band rotation makes relative offset LINEARLY decodable from the pair (p_i, p_j), so an attention head can implement an offset-selective read with one bilinear form rather than memorizing an n_max x n_max table.
features.name: Sinusoidal absolute positional encoding
features.negative_twin: Random FIXED position vectors: a non-learned table of i.i.d. vectors with matched norm and zero memory cost. This keeps 'fixed, unlearned, order-distinguishing' and removes the multi-band-rotation structure.

resource_effect.direction: ΔB_mem falls to zero (no table); ΔL_sem equals the learned table's within-range on order-sensitive obligations; ΔL_gen beyond range is better defined but not thereby better.

semantic_invariance.not_preserved: Useful behaviour outside the trained index range: the encoding is defined everywhere but the attention scores that consume it were only ever fit on the trained range, so defined is not the same as calibrated.
semantic_invariance.preserved: Order distinctions at ANY index i, including i >= n_train, since the formula is defined for all i; and the linear-shift relation between p_i and p_{i+delta}.

features.calculus_section: 13. Small-feature closure table / RoPE (S/R)
features.exact_definition: Position enters MULTIPLICATIVELY inside the score: partition the head dimension into d_h/2 planes, rotate q_i and k_j in plane m by angles i*theta_m and j*theta_m, so that <R(i)q, R(j)k> = <q, R(j-i)k> depends on (j-i) only. No vector is added to the residual stream and no position table is stored.
features.experiment: B2.2 positional necessity and geometry (rotary-like arm; relative-distance and long-extrapolation tasks)
features.gmi_type_note: R primarily: position modifies the ROUTING bilinear form rather than the carried state; S secondarily because the rotation is applied to the state coordinates Q and K.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Rotary looks free because it adds no parameters. Charge its per-token rotation FLOPs to ΔB_serve, and charge any base-frequency rescaling used to reach a longer context to ΔB_update (it is a re-calibration, not a free extension).
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: An additive relative bias b(j-i) (TF-008) supplies relative-offset dependence additively; a complex-valued attention with position-dependent phase is the same rotation written differently.
features.kill_condition: A controlled comparison at matched parameters and compute shows rotary has NO advantage on relative-distance obligations and no disadvantage on absolute-position obligations, i.e. the geometry is not the mediator.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Making the score a function of j-i by construction removes the need to LEARN translation equivariance, so the routing relation transfers across absolute positions and (subject to frequency calibration) across lengths.
features.name: RoPE / rotary position embedding
features.negative_twin: Apply the SAME per-plane rotations with angles drawn from a fixed random permutation of positions rather than from i: identical arithmetic cost, identical parameter count, and the (j-i) structure destroyed.

resource_effect.direction: ΔB_mem falls (no table); ΔL_gen on relative-distance obligations improves; ΔB_serve rises slightly (two extra multiply-adds per head-dimension pair per token).

features.calculus_section: 13. Small-feature closure table / positional encoding (S/R)
features.exact_definition: An additive term in the score: s_{ij} = q_i . k_j / sqrt(d_h) + B[bucket(j-i)] (learned scalar per bucket per head, T5-style) or s_{ij} = q_i . k_j / sqrt(d_h) - m_h (i - j) (a fixed per-head linear penalty in distance, ALiBi-style). B or m_h is read from the OFFSET only.
features.experiment: B2.2 positional necessity and geometry (relative arm) and MLX-07 dependency variability x attention/dynamic routing
features.gmi_type_note: R because the bias enters the routing score directly; S only in the weak sense that the bias table is state the model carries.
features.hidden_cost_rule: A distance penalty buys extrapolation by suppressing far attention. Meter the far-dependency obligations separately, or the extrapolation gain is bought from a task distribution that never needed the far edges.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Rotary (TF-007) obtains relative dependence multiplicatively; a sliding-window mask (TF-019) is the hard-threshold limit of a distance penalty; a learned per-head decay applied to the value stream is a third realization.
features.kill_condition: An obligation whose true dependency structure is distance-INDEPENDENT is served at least as well by a monotone distance penalty as by no bias at matched training, which would show the bias is not acting through the distance prior.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: The bias is a learned or fixed PRIOR over dependency distance added before the softmax, so it shifts routing entropy toward near tokens without removing any edge from the legal set.
features.name: Relative position bias (ALiBi / T5-style buckets)
features.negative_twin: Replace bucket(j-i) by bucket(hash(i,j)) with the same number of buckets and the same learned scalars: identical parameters and arithmetic, and the distance structure removed.

features.calculus_section: 4. Feature atlas - input representation and interface / Segment/type/modality embeddings (S,C)
features.exact_definition: An additional additive code r_i^{(0)} += S[seg(i)] where seg: positions -> a small finite set of externally supplied labels (sentence A/B, speaker, turn role, image-patch vs text token, document id). The label comes from the interface, not from the token content.
features.experiment: B2.16 instruction/preference separation (segment/role labels as the carrier of instruction structure) and MLX-17 multimodal alias breaking
features.gmi_type_note: C because the label is an interface-level declaration about the input; S because it is written into the residual coordinate.
features.hidden_cost_rule: The label is free at inference but NOT free upstream: charge the annotation/segmentation pipeline that produces seg(i) to ΔB_train, and record that serve-time behaviour now depends on a label that can be absent or wrong in deployment.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: An explicit boundary TOKEN inserted in the stream, or a block mask (TF-015) that encodes the same partition structurally, supplies the same distinction without a separate embedding table.
features.kill_condition: A segment distinction that provably does not change the protected output nonetheless improves protected performance at matched training, which would show the effect runs through optimization geometry rather than the declared distinction.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: The segment code makes an externally known boundary LINEARLY available at layer 0, so mechanisms that must condition on it (attend only within my turn; treat these tokens as image) need no depth to infer it from content.
features.name: Segment / type / modality embeddings
features.negative_twin: Randomly PERMUTE the segment labels while keeping the same number of distinct labels and the same code norms: the extra state and its cost are held and the correspondence to the real boundary is destroyed.

features.calculus_section: 5. Feature atlas - attention and routing / Q/K/V factorization (R,T)
features.exact_definition: Three independent learned linear maps of the same residual state: Q = XW^Q, K = XW^K, V = XW^V, with the score depending on (Q, K) and the transported payload on V alone. The factorization separates 'what position i is looking for' from 'what position j advertises' from 'what position j sends'.
features.experiment: B2.3 fixed vs dynamic routing (dynamic-score-select arm) and MLX-07 dependency variability x attention/dynamic routing
features.gmi_type_note: R because W^Q and W^K define the dependency-selection bilinear form X W^Q (W^K)^T X^T; T because W^V is a local transform applied to the transported content.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Score-based selection is not free: charge the n^2 d_h score computation to ΔB_serve and the discovery/search cost of the routing criterion to ΔB_search, separately from the payload transport.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: A single bilinear form with an explicitly low-rank factorization, or a kernel/linear-attention feature map phi with score phi(q).phi(k), realizes the same selection mechanism with different cost; hard kNN retrieval over K realizes its hard limit.
features.kill_condition: An obligation whose required edge sets E(x) vary strongly with x is served as cheaply by ONE fixed sparse graph as by score-based selection, at matched primitives. X-TMT3 fixes the union lower bound that makes this a decidable comparison.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Splitting selection from payload lets one head route by a LOW-rank criterion (rank <= d_h through the QK product) while sending a payload of independent content, so selection cost and payload capacity are decoupled.

features.calculus_section: 5. Feature atlas - attention and routing / Dot-product similarity and 1/sqrt(d) scaling (R,N)
features.exact_definition: The score is s_{ij} = (q_i . k_j) / sqrt(d_h) rather than q_i . k_j. Under the assumption that q and k coordinates are independent with zero mean and unit variance, Var(q.k) = d_h, so dividing by sqrt(d_h) makes the score variance O(1) independently of head width.
features.experiment: B2.6 softmax entropy/temperature (the scaling constant is the T axis at initialization)
features.gmi_type_note: N because it is a conditioning/gauge constant on the routing scores; R because those scores are the routing logits.
features.hidden_cost_rule: The constant is arithmetically free but buys an optimization regime. Charge any scale search to ΔB_search, and never report it as a semantic improvement: X-TMT4 shows a positive rescaling is exactly a temperature move.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Normalizing q and k to unit norm and using a learned scalar (QK-norm) achieves the same score-scale control; initializing W^Q with variance 1/d_h absorbs the constant exactly.
features.kill_condition: Training succeeds equally from any score scale at matched steps and matched schedule, which would show the constant is not acting through score conditioning.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: The constant keeps pre-softmax scores in the regime where softmax is neither uniform nor saturated at the initialization scale, so gradients through the attention weights are non-vanishing at the start of training.
features.name: Score scaling 1 / sqrt(d_h)
features.negative_twin: Scale by 1/d_h or by 1 instead: identical arithmetic cost, identical function class (the model can absorb any constant into W^Q), and the initialization-scale conditioning removed. The twin isolates conditioning from expressivity.

features.calculus_section: 5. Feature atlas - attention and routing / Attention temperature / logit scaling (R,D)
features.exact_definition: alpha = softmax(s / T_a) with T_a > 0. By TMT-4, softmax(s/T) = argmax_{p in Delta} [p.s + T H(p)], so T_a is exactly the weight on the entropy term of an entropy-regularized routing policy: T_a -> 0 gives hard argmax routing, T_a -> infinity gives uniform routing.
features.experiment: B2.6 softmax entropy/temperature (routing tasks with controlled ambiguity)
features.gmi_type_note: R because it parameterizes the routing distribution; D in the weak sense that at T_a -> 0 routing becomes a hard selection decision.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Temperature is free arithmetically, so it is the classic hidden knob: any comparison must FIX T_a across arms or report the search over it as ΔB_search. A tuned T_a compared against an untuned baseline is not a controlled comparison.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: A sparsemax or top-k-then-renormalize routing rule reaches comparable concentration through a different variational objective; a learned per-head scalar on the scores is the same parameter under a different name.
features.kill_condition: A single T_a is optimal across routing tasks whose source ambiguity is deliberately varied, which would falsify the entropy-vs-score trade reading of TMT-4 as the operative mechanism.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: T_a controls how much routing mass leaks to non-maximal sources. Low T_a suits obligations with an unambiguous required source; high T_a suits obligations where the answer is an average over several sources or where the score estimate is noisy.
features.name: Attention temperature T_a
features.negative_twin: Replace softmax(s/T_a) by a FIXED random distribution with the same entropy: the routing entropy is matched exactly and the score-dependence is removed, so any benefit attributed to 'the right amount of spread' is separated from 'spread on the right edges'.

features.calculus_section: 5. Feature atlas - attention and routing / Causal / padding / block / local masks (R,C)
features.exact_definition: s_{ij} <- -infinity for j > i before the softmax, so alpha_{ij} = 0 for j > i and output i is a function of x_{<=i} only. It implements the requirement that Y_i be F_i-measurable, where F_i is the legal information set at step i.
features.experiment: B2.2 / B2.3 use the masked decoder throughout; MLX-16 prediction-only causal alias registers the legality-vs-accuracy separation
features.gmi_type_note: C because it is an information-constitution declaration about what is legal to read; R because it is imposed on the routing score. It is NOT primarily a regularizer.
features.hidden_cost_rule: A masked model gets parallel training and prefix reuse for free; an unmasked one does not. Never compare their compute without charging the unmasked model for re-running the prefix, and never compare their scores without stating the legality difference.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Training a separate model per prefix length, or a recurrent/state-space update that structurally cannot see the future (TF-045), enforces the same legality with different cost.
features.kill_condition: A system that reads protected future information is judged adequate because its benchmark loss is lower. TMT-5 states this is a constitution violation regardless of the benchmark number; X-TMT5 exhibits the exact dependence that the mask removes.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: The mask removes an entire class of execution paths from the computation graph, making illegal information physically unavailable rather than merely unused; this converts a trust property into a structural one.
features.name: Causal mask
features.negative_twin: Bidirectional (unmasked) attention on the same model and data: X-TMT5 shows, in exact arithmetic, that outputs at positions < n-1 are UNCHANGED under a perturbation of the last token when the mask is present and CHANGE when it is absent.

features.calculus_section: 5. Feature atlas - attention and routing / Causal / padding / block / local masks (R,C)
features.exact_definition: s_{ij} <- -infinity on a declared index set: padding masks zero out positions beyond a sequence's true length inside a rectangular batch; document/block masks forbid attention across concatenated-document boundaries; block masks restrict attention to a declared partition of positions.
features.experiment: B2.1 (packing interacts with tokenizer length) and B2.20 parallelism/precision repricing (packing is a throughput mechanism)
features.gmi_type_note: C because the forbidden set is an interface-level declaration about what the input MEANS (this padding is not data; these two documents are unrelated); R because it is enforced on the routing scores.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Packing without masking buys throughput by leaking context. Meter cross-boundary attention mass explicitly; a throughput number reported without it is not comparable to an unpacked baseline.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Per-sequence (unpacked) batching with padding waste enforces the same independence at higher cost; resetting position indices at each document boundary enforces part of it structurally.
features.kill_condition: Removing document masks while packing leaves protected performance and robustness unchanged at matched throughput, which would show the declared independence is not doing work.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: The mask asserts an independence the interface knows and the content does not display; enforcing it prevents the model from learning spurious dependence on batch-packing artifacts (position of a document inside a packed sequence).
features.name: Padding / block / document masking
features.negative_twin: Pack documents identically but DO NOT mask across boundaries: the throughput mechanism is held exactly and the declared independence is removed, isolating the throughput gain from the contamination cost.

features.calculus_section: 13. Small-feature closure table / head count (R)
features.exact_definition: The count of parallel attention channels per layer, each with its own (W_h^Q, W_h^K, W_h^V) and its own softmax over sources. The layer output is W^O [A_1(X); ...; A_H(X)]. H is the granularity at which the layer can route by SEVERAL different criteria at once.
features.experiment: B2.4 head factorization (vary the number of independent dependency relations at matched compute/parameters)
features.gmi_type_note: R alone: H is routing-factorization granularity. It changes neither the carried state's dimension (when H d_h = d) nor the local transform.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Head count changes nothing in the FLOP budget at fixed H d_h, so it is a free-looking knob. Charge the search over H to ΔB_search and report the (H, d_h) pair, never H alone.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: A single head applied at several depths in sequence realizes multiple criteria serially; a block-diagonal wide head is arithmetically identical to H narrow heads.
features.kill_condition: Optimal H is shown to follow sequence length or parameter count alone, with no dependence on the multiplicity of required dependency relations, at matched compute.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Heads are parallel routing factors. When an obligation requires several distinct relations at the same position (syntactic antecedent AND topical source AND positional predecessor), a single normalized channel must average them; separate heads need not.
features.name: Number of heads H
features.negative_twin: H heads that all share one (W^Q, W^K) pair but keep separate W^V: the parallel-channel count and cost are identical and the distinct-criteria mechanism is removed, so any gain attributed to 'more heads' separates from 'more criteria'.

features.calculus_section: 5. Feature atlas - attention and routing / Multi-head attention (R,A1)
features.exact_definition: The full sublayer A(X) = W^O concat_h [ softmax((XW_h^Q)(XW_h^K)^T / sqrt(d_h) + M + B) X W_h^V ], i.e. H independently normalized content-addressed reads of the same sequence, concatenated and mixed by one output map W^O.
features.experiment: B2.3 fixed vs dynamic routing (all four arms) and MLX-07 dependency variability x attention/dynamic routing
features.gmi_type_note: R because it is the token-to-token dependency-selection stage; T because W^V and W^O are local transforms on the routed payload.
features.hidden_cost_rule: The n^2 score matrix is the cost. Meter it at ΔB_serve and ΔB_mem even when a tiled implementation never materializes it (TF-073 changes the IO, not the arithmetic), and meter routing DISCOVERY separately at ΔB_search.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Hard kNN retrieval over the key store, gated linear attention, or a state-space scan (TF-045) implement content-dependent mixing with different cost signatures; MoE routing (TF-083) is the same selection idea over experts instead of positions.
features.kill_condition: On an obligation family with a LARGE union-minus-mean edge gap, a fixed sparse graph matches dynamic attention at matched primitives and matched budget. That is the measurable content of TMT-3 and is the target of RV-377-056.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Content-addressed dynamic routing: the set of edges materialized on input x is chosen by x, so the layer pays for E(x) rather than for a fixed graph that must cover the union over all x (TMT-3).
features.name: Multi-head attention (the composed mechanism)
features.negative_twin: Replace the softmax weights by a FIXED (input-independent) attention pattern of the same sparsity, learned once: identical payload transport and cost, dynamic selection removed. TMT-3 predicts the loss is governed by |union_x E(x)| - E_x|E(x)|.

features.calculus_section: 5. Feature atlas - attention and routing / MHA / GQA / MQA (R,H,P)
features.exact_definition: Let H_q be the query-head count and H_kv <= H_q the number of independently materialized key/value head pairs, with query heads partitioned into H_kv groups sharing one (K, V). MHA is H_kv = H_q, MQA is H_kv = 1, GQA is intermediate. By TMT-13 the autoregressive cache holds Theta(2 L n d H_kv) elements.
features.experiment: B2.5 MHA -> GQA -> MQA (factorial: KV relation heterogeneity x sequence length x memory bandwidth price x cache capacity)
features.gmi_type_note: R because grouping constrains which routing channels may differ in what they retrieve; H because the shared K/V is the cached serving state; P because the cache size drives serving memory bandwidth.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Cache bytes are the point: report 2 L n d H_kv explicitly per arm. A quality comparison at equal PARAMETERS between MHA and MQA hides that they occupy different serving-memory budgets.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Low-rank joint compression of K and V (a latent KV) reaches the same bandwidth with a different diversity constraint; cross-layer KV sharing reduces the L factor instead of the H_kv factor.
features.kill_condition: A single H_q : H_kv ratio is optimal across obligations whose K/V heterogeneity and serving price vectors are deliberately varied, which would falsify the frontier reading of TMT-7/TMT-13 and close gap G-T04 the wrong way.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Cache size and the memory traffic per decoded token scale with H_kv, not H_q, so sharing buys serving bandwidth by spending key/value diversity. The optimum is set by how heterogeneous the required K/V maps actually are.

features.negative_twin: Keep H_kv = H_q (full MHA) but TIE the K/V parameters to a shared value by construction while still storing H_q copies: the memory cost of MHA is paid and the diversity is removed, separating 'fewer bytes' from 'fewer distinct maps'.

features.calculus_section: 5. Feature atlas - attention and routing / Sparse/sliding-window attention (R,P)
features.exact_definition: Restrict the legal source set for position i to S(i) subsetneq {0..i}: a sliding window S(i) = {i-W+1..i}, a strided/block pattern, or a window plus a few global tokens. Cost falls from Theta(n^2) to Theta(n |S|), and the model becomes a |S|-window machine at each layer (with an effective receptive field that grows with depth).
features.experiment: B2.3 fixed vs dynamic routing (fixed-sparse arm) and B2.11 context vs recurrence vs retrieval
features.gmi_type_note: R because it is a FIXED routing prior; P because the whole point is the compute/memory reduction.
features.hidden_cost_rule: The compute saving is visible and the coverage loss is not. Meter the fraction of required edges OUTSIDE the pattern per input, not just the FLOP reduction; a long context served by a narrow window is not the same object as a long context served densely.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: A distance bias with a steep slope (TF-008) is the soft version; a state-space recurrence (TF-045) compresses rather than truncates the far past; retrieval (TF-046) re-admits specific far tokens.
features.kill_condition: A fixed window matches dense attention on an obligation family constructed to have high dependency variability and a large union-minus-mean gap, at matched cost. RV-377-056 measures exactly this gap.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: A window is a hard distance prior: it is exactly right when the true dependency structure is local or recoverable, and it is TMT-3's fixed graph E_* when it is not, in which case exactness requires E_* to cover the union over all inputs.
features.name: Sparse / local / sliding-window attention
features.negative_twin: A RANDOM sparse pattern with the identical edge count and identical cost: the compute saving is held exactly and the locality prior is removed. TMT-3 predicts the difference is governed by how well the pattern covers union_x E(x).

semantic_invariance.preserved: Dependencies inside the window at every layer, and dependencies outside it that are RECOVERABLE by composition through depth (a depth-L window-W stack reaches back L(W-1) positions).

features.calculus_section: 5. Feature atlas - attention and routing / Cross-attention (R,C)
features.exact_definition: Attention whose queries come from one stream and whose keys/values come from another: Q = X_tgt W^Q, K = X_src W^K, V = X_src W^V, with X_src produced by a separately maintained encoder or memory. The two streams keep distinct state and distinct update rules.
features.experiment: B2.11 context vs recurrence vs retrieval (source-separation arm) and B2.17 RAG/tool authority
features.gmi_type_note: R because it is routing between two state collections; C because keeping the streams separate is an interface decision about what the source MEANS relative to the target.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Cross-attention looks cheap because the source encode is amortized. Report the reuse factor (target queries per source encode); at reuse 1 it is strictly more expensive than early fusion.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: A prefix (the source tokens placed in the same stream ahead of the target) reproduces the conditioning without separate state; a retrieval store (TF-046) is cross-attention with an external, mutable source.
features.kill_condition: Early fusion matches separate-stream cross-attention at matched cost on a task family where the source is reused many times per encode, which would remove the reuse mechanism as the explanation.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Maintaining separate state lets the source be encoded ONCE and read many times (and cached, versioned or replaced) instead of being re-encoded jointly with every target; the saving is the reuse factor.
features.name: Cross-attention
features.negative_twin: Early fusion: concatenate the source and target into ONE stream with full self-attention at matched total length and parameters. The routing capacity is the same or greater; only the state separation and its reuse are removed.

semantic_invariance.not_preserved: Symmetry: the target can condition on the source but not conversely, so a claim proved for early fusion (one concatenated stream) does not transfer.
semantic_invariance.preserved: The source representation: cross-attention reads X_src without modifying it, so the source stream's semantics is preserved under any number of target-side reads.

features.calculus_section: 5. Feature atlas - attention and routing / Attention dropout (R,U)
features.exact_definition: During training only, each attention weight is zeroed independently with probability p and the survivors are rescaled by 1/(1-p): alpha' = alpha . Bernoulli(1-p) / (1-p). At evaluation the identity is used, so the SERVING function is unchanged by the mechanism.
features.experiment: B2.9 normalization / B2.8 residual connection factorials include the regularization axis; MLX-10 optimizer implicit bias
features.gmi_type_note: U because it is a development-time stochastic regularizer acting on the update distribution; R because the object it perturbs is the routing distribution.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Dropout is free at serve time and costs training steps. Charge the extra steps to ΔB_train and charge the search over p to ΔB_search; a tuned-p arm against an untuned baseline is not controlled.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: DropConnect on W^Q/W^K, head dropout (dropping whole channels), or label smoothing reach related regularization through different perturbation structure; an explicit entropy penalty on alpha is the deterministic analogue.
features.kill_condition: Attention dropout improves protected performance in a regime with no overfitting and no serve-time source noise, which would rule out the redundancy mechanism.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Randomly removing routing edges during development prevents any single edge from being necessary, pushing the layer toward redundant routing that degrades gracefully when a source is absent or noisy at serve time.
features.name: Attention dropout
features.negative_twin: Add ZERO-MEAN NOISE of the same variance to the attention logits instead of dropping edges: the stochastic-perturbation magnitude is matched and the edge-removal structure is removed.

semantic_invariance.not_preserved: The training trajectory and the learned weights: two runs differing only in p reach different parameters, so nothing about the learned solution is preserved.

features.calculus_section: 6. Feature atlas - local transforms / MLPs / Position-wise MLP (T,S)
features.exact_definition: G(x) = W_2 phi(W_1 x + b_1) + b_2 applied INDEPENDENTLY and identically at every position, with W_1 in R^{d_ff x d}, W_2 in R^{d x d_ff}. It mixes across the feature axis only; it moves no information between positions.
features.experiment: B2.7 MLP width/gating (arms: linear / simple nonlinearity / gated local transform, routing need held fixed)
features.gmi_type_note: T because it is the layer's nonlinear local computation; S because it reads from and writes to the residual coordinate.
features.hidden_cost_rule: The MLP is usually the majority of both parameters and FLOPs. Report d_ff alongside d; a 'model size' that quotes only d understates serving cost by the expansion ratio.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: A depthwise/position-wise convolution of kernel 1 is the same operator; a per-position key-value memory lookup (the 'MLP as memory' reading) realizes the same map with an explicitly retrievable parameterization.
features.kill_condition: An obligation requiring per-position nonlinear composition is served equally by a rank-matched LINEAR block at matched compute, which would show the nonlinearity is not the mediator.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: After routing has gathered the relevant content into one position's residual coordinate, the MLP performs the nonlinear feature CONSTRUCTION on that coordinate; capacity added here buys per-position computation without adding token-token edges.
features.name: Position-wise MLP
features.negative_twin: Replace G by a LINEAR map W_2 W_1 of the same rank and the same FLOP count (via an explicit d_ff-dimensional bottleneck): the parameter and compute budget are matched and the nonlinearity is removed.

resource_effect.direction: All burdens rise as Theta(2 d d_ff) per token per layer (the dominant parameter and FLOP term in most decoders); ΔL_sem improves where the obligation needs per-position nonlinear composition rather than more routing.

semantic_invariance.not_preserved: Linearity of the block, hence superposition of features: phi makes the map non-additive, so 'the response to x + y is the sum of responses' is not preserved.
semantic_invariance.preserved: The position axis: applying any permutation to the sequence and then G equals applying G and then the permutation, so the MLP cannot introduce or destroy order information.

features.calculus_section: 6. Feature atlas - local transforms / MLPs / Width / expansion ratio (S,T,P)
features.exact_definition: The ratio rho = d_ff / d (conventionally 4 for an ungated MLP; near 8/3 for gated variants at matched parameters). It sets the dimension of the intermediate workspace phi(W_1 x) and hence the number of independent nonlinear features one block can construct before projecting back to d.
features.experiment: B2.7 MLP width/gating (vary local feature-composition complexity with routing need fixed)
features.gmi_type_note: S because d_ff is a (transient) state dimension; T because it bounds the local transform's capacity; P because the block's cost is 2 rho d^2 per token.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Expansion ratio is where 'parameter-matched' comparisons usually break: a gated block at rho = 4 has 1.5x the parameters of an ungated one. Match PARAMETERS and FLOPs explicitly, and say which was matched.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Two stacked narrower MLPs with the same total FLOPs, or a mixture-of-experts MLP (TF-083) that raises capacity without raising per-token FLOPs, reach comparable capacity by different means.
features.kill_condition: A single rho is optimal across obligations whose local feature-composition complexity is deliberately varied at fixed routing demand, which would close gap G-T06 against the frontier reading.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: rho is the local-workspace-versus-compute frontier: widening buys more independent nonlinear features per block at linear cost in FLOPs, and is dominated by adding depth once feature construction is no longer the binding constraint.
features.name: MLP width / expansion ratio
features.negative_twin: Hold rho and hold FLOPs but make W_1 BLOCK-DIAGONAL with the same number of nonzeros arranged so the intermediate units cannot mix input coordinates freely: workspace size is nominally matched and its usable capacity is cut.

resource_effect.direction: All three burdens rise linearly in rho; ΔL_sem improves only while local-feature capacity binds.

semantic_invariance.preserved: The residual stream dimension d and therefore the interface to every other mechanism: rho changes the block's internals only.

features.calculus_section: 6. Feature atlas - local transforms / MLPs / ReLU / GELU / SiLU (T,U)
features.exact_definition: The elementwise nonlinearity phi in the MLP: ReLU(x) = max(0, x); GELU(x) = x Phi(x) with Phi the standard normal CDF; SiLU/Swish(x) = x sigma(x). All three are monotone, unbounded above, bounded below, and agree asymptotically; they differ in smoothness at 0 and in whether small negative inputs pass a small signal.
features.experiment: B2.7 MLP width/gating (activation arm) and MLX-10 optimizer implicit bias
features.gmi_type_note: T because phi is the local nonlinearity; U because its derivative shape is what the optimizer sees (ReLU has a dead region with exactly zero gradient; GELU and SiLU do not).
features.hidden_cost_rule: Activation choice changes serving cost (transcendental vs compare) and can change the numerically safe precision. Charge both, and never report an activation swap as a semantic capability change.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: A hard-sigmoid gated unit, a learned-parameter activation (PReLU), or a low-order polynomial approximation at matched response range all reproduce the response geometry at different serving cost.
features.kill_condition: Matched-shape activations with and without a dead region train identically at matched width and schedule, which would remove the gradient-profile mechanism and leave the choice arbitrary.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: The activation's derivative profile determines how many units receive gradient early in training and how sharply the response bends; the claimed advantage of smooth activations is fewer permanently dead units, not greater expressivity.
features.name: Activation function (ReLU / GELU / SiLU)
features.negative_twin: A PIECEWISE-LINEAR approximation of GELU with the same values at a fixed grid and the same serving cost: the response shape is matched and the exact smoothness is removed, isolating 'shape' from 'smoothness'.

semantic_invariance.not_preserved: The optimization trajectory and the induced feature geometry: the dead-unit behaviour of ReLU and the smooth small-negative response of GELU/SiLU give different gradient flows from the same initialization.

features.calculus_section: 6. Feature atlas - local transforms / MLPs / GLU / SwiGLU-like gates (T,R)
features.exact_definition: A multiplicative local gate: G(x) = W_2 ( phi(W_g x) (elementwise product) W_1 x ), with three matrices instead of two. SwiGLU takes phi = SiLU. At matched parameter count d_ff is reduced by about 2/3 relative to an ungated block.
features.experiment: B2.7 MLP width/gating (gated local transform arm, matched parameter/FLOP controls)
features.gmi_type_note: T because it is still a per-position transform; R because the elementwise product is content-conditioned selection AMONG local features - micro-routing inside the block.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Gating is the canonical place where 'matched parameters' and 'matched FLOPs' disagree. State which was held; a gated block compared at equal d_ff has 1.5x the compute of its baseline.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: A depth-2 ungated MLP can approximate the product; a bilinear layer without the phi is the ungated GLU; a per-feature attention gate computes the same conditional selection through the routing path instead.
features.kill_condition: A gated block shows no advantage over an ungated block on obligations requiring conditional local computation once parameters AND FLOPs are matched, which would close gap G-T06 against the gating reading.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Gating lets the value carried by one feature be switched on or off by ANOTHER feature computed from the same coordinate, so a conditional local computation needs one block rather than a depth-2 construction.
features.name: GLU / SwiGLU gating
features.negative_twin: Replace the gate phi(W_g x) by a LEARNED CONSTANT vector g (same shape, same multiply, no input dependence): the extra parameters and the elementwise multiply are kept and the content-conditioning is removed.

semantic_invariance.preserved: Position independence and the residual interface: the gate mixes nothing across positions.

features.calculus_section: 7. Feature atlas - residual stream and normalization / Residual connection (S,U)
features.exact_definition: y = x + f(x) around every sublayer, so the Jacobian is J_y = I + J_f and a depth-L stack has end-to-end Jacobian prod_l (I + J_{f_l}). The sublayer computes an INCREMENT to a carried state rather than replacing it.
features.experiment: B2.8 residual connection (vary depth and perturbation magnitude; shallow-regime negative control)
features.gmi_type_note: S because the identity path makes the residual stream a persistent carried coordinate; U because the identity term is what the backward pass propagates.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Skips are nearly free in FLOPs and not free in activation memory. Charge the retained skip tensors to ΔB_mem, and do not credit residuals with capability gains that are really depth gains they made reachable.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: A gated/highway skip y = g(x) x + (1-g(x)) f(x), a fixed-scale skip y = alpha x + f(x), or a dense (DenseNet-style) concatenation supply an identity-carrying path with different scaling behaviour.
features.kill_condition: A deep stack without skips trains as well as one with skips at matched depth, width and schedule, or a residual stack is shown stable for arbitrary J_f - either would break the Jacobian-identity reading. X-TMT9 fixes the algebra at its scope.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: The explicit identity term in every layer's Jacobian gives a gradient path that does not pass through any learned matrix, so signal reaches early layers at depth where a plain product prod_l J_{f_l} would have vanished.
features.name: Residual connection
features.negative_twin: The identical stack WITHOUT the skip (y = f(x)) at the same depth, width and initialization. X-TMT9 computes both end-to-end Jacobians in exact rational arithmetic: the residual product stays near I while the plain product contracts.

semantic_invariance.not_preserved: Boundedness of the end-to-end Jacobian: prod_l (I + J_{f_l}) can still blow up or collapse when the J_{f_l} are large or aligned, so 'residuals guarantee trainability' is false.
semantic_invariance.preserved: The ability of the block to act as the identity: setting f = 0 leaves the state untouched, so a residual stack can always represent a shallower one exactly.

features.calculus_section: 7. Feature atlas - residual stream and normalization / Residual stream (S,H)
features.exact_definition: The sequence of vectors r^{(0)}, ..., r^{(L)} in R^{n x d} that every sublayer reads from and adds to. Because writes are additive into one d-dimensional space, features written by different mechanisms SUPERPOSE, and any read is a linear functional of the sum.
features.experiment: MLX-41 probe vs causal-use separation and MLX-42 mechanism witness invariance; gap G-T08 residual-stream superposition/interference law
features.gmi_type_note: S because it is the coordinate system of the whole model; H because it is the fast working memory through which mechanisms at different depths communicate within one forward pass.
features.hidden_cost_rule: The stream is where 'my probe found feature X' becomes an unpriced claim. Charge every interpretability claim with a causal intervention (MLX-41), and charge n d L activation bytes to ΔB_mem.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Concatenation-based state (each layer appends its own coordinates) removes superposition at linear memory cost; a bottlenecked read/write with per-layer projections reproduces the sharing with an explicit capacity constraint.
features.kill_condition: A model is shown to carry, without measurable interference, a number of simultaneously active linearly-readable features far exceeding d, which would contradict the bandwidth reading.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: The stream is a bandwidth-limited shared bus. Interference between concurrently carried features is the cost of the bus; superposition is what lets a width-d model carry more than d features when they are rarely simultaneously active.
features.name: Residual stream (as shared state)
features.negative_twin: Force each sublayer to write into a DISJOINT slice of the width (no shared directions, same total width, same parameters): the bus is partitioned, superposition is impossible, and the interference mechanism is removed.

semantic_invariance.not_preserved: One-feature-per-direction: when more features are carried than d, directions must be shared, so linear readability of any single feature without interference is NOT preserved.
semantic_invariance.preserved: Additive decomposability: the stream at layer l is exactly the sum of the embedding and every sublayer's write up to l, so the path decomposition is exact.

features.calculus_section: 7. Feature atlas - residual stream and normalization / LayerNorm (N,U)
features.exact_definition: LN(x) = gamma (x - mu(x)) / sqrt(sigma^2(x) + eps) + beta with mu and sigma^2 the mean and variance over the d feature coordinates of a single position. It is exactly invariant to x -> a x + b 1 for a > 0 (up to eps), then re-parameterized by learned gamma, beta.
features.experiment: B2.9 normalization (factorial: depth x activation-scale drift x precision x batch/sequence statistics; arms none / center+scale / RMS-like)
features.gmi_type_note: N because it imposes a gauge (per-position shift and scale) on the state; U because that gauge changes the loss surface the optimizer traverses.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Normalization is cheap in FLOPs and expensive in memory traffic and in precision requirements. Charge the reduction's bandwidth to ΔB_serve, and record eps and the accumulation precision (TF-031) with any exactness claim.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: RMSNorm (TF-029) drops the recentering; a fixed scaling schedule per depth reproduces the conditioning without per-input statistics; weight normalization moves the gauge onto the parameters instead of the activations.
features.kill_condition: A deep stack trains equally well with no normalization at matched depth, learning rate schedule and precision, which would remove the conditioning mediator and leave normalization an arbitrary convention.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Removing scale and shift drift makes the effective input distribution of each sublayer stationary across depth and across training steps, which conditions the optimization problem; the learned gamma, beta restore the expressivity the gauge removed.
features.name: LayerNorm
features.negative_twin: Replace LN by a FIXED affine map with the same gamma, beta and a constant divisor equal to the average observed sigma: the arithmetic shape and the parameters are kept and the per-input normalization is removed.

resource_effect.direction: ΔB_train falls (larger stable learning rates, less depth-dependent drift); ΔB_serve rises by the mean/variance reduction and the division; ΔL_rob improves against input-scale shift.

semantic_invariance.not_preserved: Relative magnitude information across positions and across layers: LN discards the per-position norm, so an obligation that depends on absolute activation scale is not preserved.
semantic_invariance.preserved: Per-position affine gauge: the output is unchanged (as eps -> 0) by adding a constant to all coordinates or by rescaling them, so any claim about activation scale upstream of LN is not observable downstream.

features.calculus_section: 7. Feature atlas - residual stream and normalization / RMSNorm (N,U,P)
features.exact_definition: RMS(x) = gamma x / sqrt(mean(x^2) + eps): the same per-position scale gauge as LayerNorm with the recentering (subtracting mu) and usually the bias beta removed. It is invariant to x -> a x for a > 0 but NOT to x -> x + b 1.
features.experiment: B2.9 normalization (RMS-like arm, same factorial)
features.gmi_type_note: N/U as for LayerNorm; P additionally, because dropping the mean pass removes one reduction over d per position and one elementwise subtraction, which matters at serving bandwidth.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Report the normalizer WITH its eps and accumulation dtype. An RMSNorm-for-LayerNorm swap is a serving-cost change; presenting the resulting throughput gain as a model improvement is an implementation-label error (TMT-7).
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: LayerNorm with beta frozen at zero and the mean empirically near zero is functionally close; scaled weight normalization moves the same gauge to the parameters.
features.kill_condition: An obligation is found where the per-position MEAN of the residual stream is load-bearing and RMSNorm therefore degrades protected performance while LayerNorm does not - or, conversely, RMSNorm is shown to help beyond its cost saving.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: If the residual stream's per-position mean carries no obligation-relevant information, recentering is pure cost; RMSNorm is the cheaper gauge that keeps the scale control and discards the unused shift control.
features.name: RMSNorm
features.negative_twin: LayerNorm with the recentering computed but then ADDED BACK (compute mu, subtract it, then add it): identical cost to LayerNorm, identical function to RMSNorm-with-bias, isolating 'the cost of recentering' from 'the effect of recentering'.

features.calculus_section: 7. Feature atlas - residual stream and normalization / Pre-norm vs post-norm (N,U)
features.exact_definition: Pre-norm: x_{l+1} = x_l + f_l(N(x_l)), so the identity path from input to output is normalization-free. Post-norm: x_{l+1} = N(x_l + f_l(x_l)), so every skip passes through a normalizer. The two give different end-to-end Jacobians: pre-norm keeps an exact identity term at every depth, post-norm does not.
features.experiment: B2.10 pre/post norm (optimization stability vs depth and residual magnitude)
features.gmi_type_note: N/U: the placement is a pure update-geometry decision; it changes neither parameter count nor FLOPs.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Placement is free in FLOPs and buys schedule. Charge the warmup steps a post-norm stack needs to ΔB_train; comparing pre-norm with warmup against post-norm without it is not a controlled comparison.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: A residual scaling factor alpha_l (DeepNet-style or a learned per-layer scale) applied to post-norm reproduces the pre-norm Jacobian condition without moving the normalizer; a final-only normalizer is a third placement.
features.kill_condition: Post-norm trains as easily as pre-norm at large depth with no warmup and the same learning rate, which would remove the Jacobian-composition mediator.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Pre-norm preserves the exact identity term of TMT-9 through arbitrary depth; post-norm multiplies the skip by the normalizer's Jacobian at every layer, so gradient magnitude at depth depends on the accumulated normalizer geometry.
features.name: Pre-norm vs post-norm placement
features.negative_twin: Post-norm with the normalizer's gain FROZEN to the identity at initialization: placement is post-norm, the initial Jacobian is pre-norm-like, so the placement effect separates from the initialization effect.

features.calculus_section: 7. Feature atlas - residual stream and normalization / epsilon constants / clipping (N,U)
features.exact_definition: The additive eps inside every normalizer's sqrt, the clamp applied to logits or activations (clip(x, -c, c)), and the denominator floors in the optimizer (Adam's eps). Each replaces an exactly-defined but numerically unstable operation with a nearby bounded one, at a bias whose size is set by the constant.
features.experiment: B2.9 normalization (precision axis of the factorial) and B2.14 quantization / distillation
features.gmi_type_note: N because these are conditioning constants on the state and its statistics; U because Adam's eps and clipping change the update law itself.
features.hidden_cost_rule: These constants are almost never reported and they change results. Record eps, clip bounds and accumulation dtype in every receipt; an 'exact' claim that does not state them is not checkable (X-TMT12 is the general form of the collision they can cause).
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Higher-precision accumulation (TF-075) removes the need for a large eps; a smooth soft-clip (tanh-based) replaces the hard clamp with a bounded map of the same range.
features.kill_condition: An eps or clip value is shown optimal independently of the numeric format and the activation statistics, which would make it a semantic rather than a numerical constant.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: These constants set the precision at which a degenerate case stops being handled exactly. Their optimum is a function of the numeric format and the activation statistics, not of the task semantics.
features.name: Epsilon constants and value clipping
features.negative_twin: Run the identical model with eps and clips set to their degenerate limits (eps -> 0, c -> infinity) in WIDE arithmetic: the semantics is the unguarded one and the numerical hazard is removed by precision instead of by a constant, separating the two.

features.calculus_section: 13. Small-feature closure table (initialization enters through the update-geometry rows)
features.exact_definition: The distribution from which Theta_0 is drawn: Glorot/Xavier (variance 2/(fan_in + fan_out)), He/Kaiming (2/fan_in, matched to ReLU), small-scale output-projection init (often scaled by 1/sqrt(2L) in deep decoders), and zero-init for biases and for the final projection of each residual branch.
features.experiment: B2.8 residual connection / B2.10 pre-post norm factorials both vary initialization scale; MLX-11 lazy/kernel vs feature-learning regime
features.gmi_type_note: U because Theta_0 is the starting point of the development trajectory and fixes the early gradient scale; S because it sets the initial geometry of the state coordinates.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Initialization is free at serve time and decides training cost. Record the scheme and the seed; a result that depends on an unreported init is not reproducible, and seed variance must be reported alongside any claimed difference.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Orthogonal initialization at the same scale, a data-dependent (LSUV-style) rescaling pass, or a normalizer that enforces the same forward variance at run time reach the same conditioning by different means.
features.kill_condition: Training outcome at a fixed budget is invariant to the initialization scale across depths, which would remove the signal-scale mechanism and make the scheme cosmetic.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Initialization sets the forward and backward variance at every depth. A scheme that keeps both near 1 across L layers gives non-degenerate gradients at step 0; a residual-branch init near zero makes the stack start as the identity and grow function gradually.
features.name: Initialization scheme
features.negative_twin: The same scheme with the same variance but a FIXED SEED-INDEPENDENT rank-deficient draw (e.g. all rows equal within a layer): the scale is matched exactly and the symmetry-breaking is removed.

features.calculus_section: 8. Feature atlas - output and decoding / Unembedding / tied input-output embeddings (C,S)
features.exact_definition: Impose W_U = E^T (or more generally theta_1 = theta_2 for two otherwise independent parameter blocks). By TMT-8 the tied family is a SUBSET of the untied family: F_tied subseteq F_untied, with the inclusion strict in general.
features.experiment: B2.6 / MLX-06 symmetry x parameter sharing
features.gmi_type_note: S because it constrains the state coordinates to serve both the read-in and the read-out role; C because both maps are compiler interfaces between symbols and coordinates.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Tying is reported as free parameters saved. Charge the lost degrees of freedom: report the tied and untied arms at matched TOTAL parameters, not matched d, or the saving and the constraint are conflated.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: A tied pair plus a learned low-rank correction W_U = E^T + AB recovers the untied freedom at controlled cost; tying with a learned diagonal rescaling is an intermediate constraint.
features.kill_condition: A tied family is shown to express a function outside the untied family with the same parameterization, contradicting TMT-8. X-TMT8 enumerates a tiny two-layer family and verifies both the inclusion and its strictness.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Tying halves the vocabulary parameter count and forces the same similarity geometry on read-in and read-out, which is the right prior when the obligation is symmetric in that sense and a bias cost when it is not.
features.name: Weight tying (input embedding / unembedding)
features.negative_twin: Untied embeddings with the SAME total parameter count (halve d for both tables): the parameter saving is matched exactly and the symmetry constraint is removed, separating 'fewer parameters' from 'this particular equality'.

features.calculus_section: 9. Feature atlas - autoregressive objective and training protocol / dropout / stochastic depth (U,S)
features.exact_definition: Dropout zeroes each unit of a hidden activation independently with probability p during training and rescales by 1/(1-p). Stochastic depth does the same at the SUBLAYER level: with probability p_l the whole residual branch is skipped, so x_{l+1} = x_l. Both are identity at evaluation.
features.experiment: B2.8 residual connection (depth x perturbation factorial) and MLX-12 overparameterization and optimization accessibility
features.gmi_type_note: U because both are development-time stochastic subrealization sampling; S because what is perturbed is the carried state.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Both are serve-time free and train-time costly; stochastic depth also changes the effective depth seen per step. Charge the extra steps to ΔB_train and report the EXPECTED depth, not the nominal one.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Weight decay (TF-061), data augmentation, or an explicit ensemble of narrower models reach related regularization; layer-drop at inference time (a different mechanism) turns stochastic depth into a serving compiler instead.
features.kill_condition: Dropout or stochastic depth improves protected performance in a regime with no overfitting at matched training steps, which would remove the redundancy mechanism as the explanation.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Random subrealization forces the surviving units/branches to be individually sufficient, which spreads the represented function over redundant paths rather than concentrating it in a few fragile ones.
features.name: Dropout and stochastic depth
features.negative_twin: Additive Gaussian noise on the same activations with matched variance: the perturbation magnitude is held and the subnetwork-sampling structure is removed.

features.calculus_section: 8. Feature atlas - output and decoding / Softmax output (D)
features.exact_definition: z_i = W_U N_f(r_i^{(L)}) in R^V, then p(x_{i+1} | x_{<=i}) = softmax(z_i / T_d). The unembedding is the compiler back from the continuous residual coordinate to the discrete alphabet; the softmax makes the result a normalized categorical distribution.
features.experiment: MLX-27 abstention vs unsafe serving and MLX-32 emergence metric audit (both turn on the distribution, not the argmax)
features.gmi_type_note: C because W_U is the read-out interface to the symbol alphabet; D because the normalized distribution is the object every decision policy consumes.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Vd parameters and a V-way normalization per step are the serving cost. Report them separately from the body, and state T_d with every probability: an uncalibrated probability quoted without T_d is not a measurement.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: A hierarchical or sampled softmax computes the same distribution with different cost; a normalizing-flow or energy-based head is a different realization of the same normalization obligation.
features.kill_condition: A calibration claim is shown to be invariant to the decoding temperature, which would collapse the accuracy/calibration distinction this entry rests on.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: The softmax turns an unnormalized compatibility score into a proper distribution, which is what makes the cross-entropy objective (TF-054) a proper scoring rule and what makes calibration a separately checkable obligation from accuracy.
features.name: Unembedding and output softmax
features.negative_twin: Replace the softmax by an unnormalized score and take the argmax directly: accuracy is preserved exactly and the distribution (and therefore calibration, sampling and the cross-entropy signal) is removed.

features.calculus_section: 8. Feature atlas - output and decoding / Temperature / top-k / top-p (D)
features.exact_definition: A decoder D maps the model distribution p_theta, a prompt and any search/random state to an emitted sequence. By TMT-15 the pair (p_theta, D) determines behaviour, and D can be changed with theta untouched, so 'the model improved' and 'the decoder improved' are different claims about different objects.
features.experiment: B2.18 chain-of-thought/test-time working state and B2.19 speculative decoding both hold theta fixed and vary D; MLX-37 planning vs compiled policy
features.gmi_type_note: D alone: the decoder is the action-selection stage. It reads the predictive state but changes no parameter and no stored knowledge.
features.hidden_cost_rule: State the decoder (and its temperature, k, p, beam width and sample count) with EVERY reported number. An evaluation that names only the model is not attributable, and its compute is not comparable.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Any of TF-037..TF-042 instantiates D; a constrained/grammar decoder and a verifier-gated decoder (TF-043, TF-069) are decoders with an admission rule attached.
features.kill_condition: A measured improvement is shown to be attributable to p_theta while the decoder differed between arms, i.e. the two objects are shown not to be separable. X-TMT15 establishes the separation on an exact finite scope.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: The decoder selects a point (or a set) from a distribution the model already defines. All of its effect is in the selection rule; none of it is in what the model knows.
features.name: Decoding policy (the decision object)
features.negative_twin: The SAME decoder applied to a p_theta obtained by a different training run, and the SAME p_theta decoded by a different decoder: running both arms is the only way to attribute a measured change to one object.

features.calculus_section: 8. Feature atlas - output and decoding / Temperature / top-k / top-p (D)
features.exact_definition: Sample x_{t+1} ~ softmax(z_t / T_d). T_d -> 0 is greedy argmax; T_d = 1 is the model's own distribution; T_d > 1 flattens it. By TMT-4 this is the same entropy-regularized family as attention temperature, applied to the output decision instead of to routing.
features.experiment: B2.18 (test-time working state at controlled total compute) and MLX-27 abstention vs unsafe serving
features.gmi_type_note: D alone. It changes no parameter, no cached state and no stored knowledge; it reweights the decision over an unchanged distribution.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Temperature is free in FLOPs, so it is the easiest hidden knob in any comparison. Fix it across arms or charge the search to ΔB_search; report T_d with every generation metric.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Top-k (TF-038) and top-p (TF-039) reach comparable concentration by truncation rather than by rescaling; a Mirostat-style controller targets an entropy level directly.
features.kill_condition: A single T_d is optimal for both single-sample accuracy and best-of-N coverage on the same obligation, which would collapse the quality/diversity trade.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: T_d trades expected per-sample quality against sample diversity. Low T_d concentrates on the mode (better single-sample accuracy, worse coverage); high T_d spreads mass (better coverage for best-of-N, worse single samples).
features.name: Sampling temperature T_d
features.negative_twin: Sample from a FIXED distribution with the same entropy as softmax(z/T_d) but ignoring z: entropy is matched and the score-dependence removed, separating 'more diversity' from 'diversity in the right places'.

features.calculus_section: 8. Feature atlas - output and decoding / Temperature / top-k / top-p (D)
features.exact_definition: Keep only the k highest-probability tokens, set the rest to zero, renormalize, then sample: p'(x) proportional to p(x) 1[x in TopK_k(p)]. k = 1 is exactly greedy decoding.
features.experiment: B2.18 test-time working state; MLX-27 abstention vs unsafe serving (truncation is a crude admission rule)
features.gmi_type_note: D alone: a hard admission rule over the decision alphabet at each step.
features.hidden_cost_rule: Truncation silently changes the served distribution. Any perplexity or calibration number must be computed under the UNTRUNCATED p_theta, or reported explicitly as a property of the truncated decoder (TMT-15).
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Top-p (TF-039) adapts the retained set size to the step's entropy; epsilon-sampling (drop below an absolute probability floor) is a third truncation rule; k = 1 coincides with greedy.
features.kill_condition: A fixed k is optimal across steps whose entropy is deliberately varied, which would remove the entropy-mismatch objection and make top-p's adaptivity pointless.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Truncation removes the low-probability tail that accumulates over many steps into a high chance of at least one bad token, at the cost of making a fixed number of options available regardless of how peaked or flat the step actually is.
features.name: Top-k truncation
features.negative_twin: Keep a RANDOM k-subset of the vocabulary (excluding the argmax to avoid triviality) and renormalize: the support size is matched exactly and the ranking is removed.

features.calculus_section: 8. Feature atlas - output and decoding / Temperature / top-k / top-p (D)
features.exact_definition: Keep the smallest set S of highest-probability tokens with sum_{x in S} p(x) >= p, renormalize over S, then sample. The retained set size |S| ADAPTS to the step: it is 1 at a fully peaked step and large at a flat one.
features.experiment: B2.18 test-time working state; MLX-27 abstention vs unsafe serving
features.gmi_type_note: D alone, like top-k, but with a mass-based rather than a count-based admission rule.
features.hidden_cost_rule: As for top-k: report p and state that likelihood-based metrics are computed under the untruncated distribution. Comparing a top-p arm's text quality against a greedy arm's perplexity compares two different objects.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Top-k (TF-038) with k tuned per domain approximates it when step entropy is homogeneous; a typical-sampling rule truncates by information content rather than by mass.
features.kill_condition: Top-p shows no advantage over a well-tuned top-k on a corpus with deliberately heterogeneous step entropy, which would remove the adaptivity mechanism.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Conditioning the retained set on the step's own probability mass matches the admission rule to the model's own confidence, so confident steps are effectively greedy and uncertain steps stay diverse without a global k.
features.name: Top-p (nucleus) truncation
features.negative_twin: Truncate to a set of the SAME SIZE |S| as top-p would choose at each step, but pick it at random among non-argmax tokens: the adaptive set size is matched step by step and the ranking is removed.

semantic_invariance.preserved: The relative probabilities within the nucleus and the argmax (always retained).

features.calculus_section: 8. Feature atlas - output and decoding / Beam search (D,P)
features.exact_definition: Maintain B partial sequences; at each step expand every beam by every token, score by the accumulated log p_theta (optionally length-normalized), and keep the best B. It is a bounded-width search for the sequence argmax, which greedy decoding does NOT find in general.
features.experiment: B2.19 speculative decoding shares the serving-economics frame; MLX-37 planning vs compiled policy
features.gmi_type_note: D because it is a decision/search policy over sequences; P because the B-fold widening is a real serving-compute and serving-memory multiplier (B copies of the KV cache).
features.hidden_cost_rule: Beam multiplies serving compute AND cache memory by B. Report B with every quality number and charge B-fold ΔB_serve; a beam-B result compared against a greedy baseline at 'the same model' is a B-fold compute comparison.
features.implementation_equivalent_alternative: Best-of-N sampling with likelihood reranking (TF-041) approximates the same objective stochastically; A*-style or MCTS decoding (TF-042) allocates the same search budget non-uniformly.
features.kill_condition: Greedy is shown to find the sequence argmax for the model class in question, which would make beam search pure overhead. X-TMT15 exhibits a counterexample in exact arithmetic at its scope.
features.mechanism_hypothesis: Greedy commits at each step to the locally best token and cannot recover from a high-probability prefix that leads only to low-probability continuations; beam defers the commitment across B alternatives, so it finds higher-likelihood sequences.
features.name: Beam search
features.negative_twin: Sample B independent continuations at T_d = 1 and keep the one with highest log p_theta: identical compute, identical selection criterion, and the shared-prefix pruning structure of beam removed.
